statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). NQ front month is quoted at 29,035.50, down 1.20%, and has recovered to about 74% of the 28,816.25-29,111.00 session range after trading near 22% an hour ago. The 28,816.25 low has now held for more than four hours, the 1.63% cash gap has been absorbed rather than extended, and VIX has decayed to 17.21, its session low, from 17.86. Tail falls five points to 21. Crude remains the outstanding amplifier, with WTI at $104.27 and up 4.21%.
recommendation: Tail at 21 sits in the watch band, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window moves to 19:00-20:00 UTC, covering the final cash hour, because the opening liquidity transfer that justified the earlier 13:00-16:00 UTC window has now been observed and absorbed. Conditional Tail peaks at 23 in that power hour, two points below the block mapping, eases into the low band across the thin overnight and Asian sessions, and returns to the watch band during Tuesday's European midday and the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC US releases. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: The opening gap is absorbed: NQ recovers to roughly 74% of its session range from 22% an hour ago while VIX decays to a 17.21 session low; Tail falls to 21 and the danger window moves to the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour
body:
The failing retracement recorded in the 13:00 UTC assessment has resolved in the opposite direction. As of 14:20 UTC, NQ front month is quoted at 29,035.50, down 351.50 points or 1.20% against a 29,387.00 reference, having traded as low as 28,816.25 and as high as 29,111.00. The contract now sits about 219 points above the session low, roughly 74% of the session range, against about 22% one hour ago. The Nasdaq-100 cash index tells the same story from a different feed: it opened at 28,890.93 after a 1.63% gap against Friday's 29,368.44 close, set its low at 28,867.67 in the first minutes, and has since traded to 29,074.11 and back to 28,982.73, down 1.31%. Both feeds show a two-way cash session with a completed retracement rather than the persistent one-way extension that would deny mean reversion.

The volatility evidence points the same way. VIX is quoted at 17.21, up 8.64% on the day against a 15.84 close, but it is trading at the bottom of its 17.17 to 18.17 session range rather than rebuilding toward the high. Implied volatility that peaks into a gap-down open and then decays through the first cash hour is the signature of an orderly liquidity transfer, and it is the single clearest difference from the picture an hour ago. The 28,816.25 futures low set around 10:15 UTC has now survived more than four hours across the European session, the cash open and the first cash hour. Tail falls five points to 21, returning the mapping to the watch band.

The catalyst stack behind the original move is unchanged and remains verified, which is why Tail eases rather than collapsing into the low band. OilPrice reports that Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the primary export route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, remains shut after drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory damaged multiple pumping stations, with traders estimating that up to 4% of global supply could be lost if it is not reopened. The same report describes a Houthi missile and drone attack on a military base at Sharurah, a vessel struck near Qeshm Island inside the strait, and a postponed Gulf-Iran meeting on temporary shipping arrangements. WTI has extended to $104.27, up 4.21%, with Brent at $109.23, up 4.41%, a four-month high. Separately, CNN reports that an essay from Anthropic's chief executive urging a slower pace of AI capability advancement, publicly endorsed by the heads of xAI and OpenAI, drove SoftBank about 11% lower at the Tokyo close, the Kospi down 3.3%, SK Hynix down 6.4% and ASML down about 6%.

Two amplifiers therefore remain live while the price-path amplifier has faded. Crude is still extending rather than stabilising, and the 10-year yield at 4.996% is up 2.1 basis points and pressing the 5% level, so rates are not cushioning equities. Against that, the strategy-relevant question is whether the tape denies mean reversion, and the observed answer over the past hour is that it has not: the gap was absorbed, the low held, the range is 295 points wide with price in its upper quarter, and implied volatility decayed. Consistent with the published risk definitions, event importance, surprise magnitude and an unresolved supply mechanism raise Stress and keep Confidence honest rather than forcing Tail higher once the observed path shows orderly discovery. Stress eases three points to 76, still in the high band.

The danger window moves to 19:00 to 20:00 UTC, the final cash hour. The earlier window covering the 13:30 UTC open has served its purpose and the transition it protected is now observed. The power hour is the remaining scheduled point at which a gap-down day either confirms absorption into the settlement or reverses it, and it is also when a late crude headline would meet the thinnest liquidity of the cash session. Conditional Tail peaks at 23 there, two points below the block mapping, and that elevation reflects a scheduled transition and the live amplifier count rather than any observed closing structure. Confidence is 88: the price, volatility, rates, energy, catalyst and calendar evidence is current and verified from primary sources, with the 2-year yield the one gap, last published officially at 4.56% for 10 September in the Federal Reserve H.15 release. The shared cross-asset context file was collected at 07:12 UTC, more than seven hours before this assessment, and carried a partial collection status with an unavailable calendar section, so it was treated as stale and was not used as evidence.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the Claude series ran through the low band during Sunday's US evening, entered the watch band from 21:00 UTC as the AI-slowdown and Middle East supply stories developed, and reached the elevated band at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC when NQ set a sequence of lower lows into 28,816.25 with a trend-down mode. It stepped back to the watch band at 11:00 and 12:00 UTC, then returned to the elevated band at 13:00 UTC when the bounce faded to about 22% of the session range into the cash open. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 69 and 79, and Confidence improved from 85 to 88 as live price evidence became available. All 24 hourly slots are available from published Claude history.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook is built around an opening gap that has now been absorbed. Conditional Tail holds at 21 through the second cash hour, eases to 20 across the US midday, and peaks at 23 in the 19:00 UTC power hour that forms the published danger window. It then decays into the low band from 21:00 UTC across the thin post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, with small uplifts in the hours where crude typically reprices first on Middle East developments. The path returns toward the watch band during Tuesday's European midday and US pre-market, and reaches 22 for the 12:15 UTC ADP and 12:30 UTC Empire State releases, three points below the block mapping. Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last verified price observation at 14:20 UTC. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not observed structure.
